note: Re-judged 2026-11-14 by an independent auditor who authored neither 08fe903803 nor the uncommitted phase 2 of spec-single-owner-lifecycle-2-bgp-session. RFC 4724 Section 4 read: "The End-of-RIB marker MUST be sent by a BGP speaker to its peer once it completes the initial routing update (including the case when there is no update to send) for an address family after the BGP session is established." Units read: TestInitialSyncEORReachesTheSilentFamilyToo, TestInitialSyncEORSentWhenNeitherSideDeclaredAFamily, TestInitialSyncMarkerWaitsForNoProcess, TestInitialSyncShutsTheQueueGateAndFreesTheRailsWithTheMarker, TestRFC4724EndOfRIBNotSentBeforeTheInitialUpdateCompletes (sync call only). New tag TestPredecessorSyncWritesNothingOnSuccessor (rfc4724_rapid_reconnect_test.go, positive): a first session ends by Cease while its sync waits in an unacknowledged peer-up barrier; the second session, with one route queued, must carry exactly one UPDATE with that route (require.Len 1, NLRI bytes match), then the exact IPv4 unicast End-of-RIB (bytes.Equal eorUpdate), then no UPDATE for syncJoinProbe (requireNoUpdateAfter), so a predecessor's marker or route on the successor, a lost route or a missing marker goes red; its claim says no more than that body. checkNoFamilyEndOfRIB changed only how it polls (3s interval, last observation kept when an identity read is cut, FRR version line); its assertions still require FRR's own bgp_update_receive_eor decode on the original session after the route arrived. 08fe903803 moved the initial-sync gate (sendingInitialRoutes) and the End-of-RIB owed mark (initialSyncEOROwed) from Peer onto Session. In the tagged units named stale it replaced peer.sendInitialRoutes() with peer.runInitialSyncNow(), which is Peer.sendInitialRoutes(p.testInitialSync()) (initial_sync_helpers_test.go): the same production sync body, run on the session the fixture installed (or one built with NewSession(p.settings) and published through establishedSession as enterEstablished does); it replaced peer.<flag>.Store(v) with peer.testInitialSync().<flag>.Store(v) or setTestInitialSync, and drainAndCloseQueueGate now takes that session. git diff 08fe903803^ against the working tree shows no assertion, expected byte, driven input or tag prose changed in any of them, each under the RFC-approved line 08fe903803 carries. Questions 1, 3 and 4 answer exactly as the earlier judgement below; question 2 still rests on the same producers, whose discrimination records are retaken by ./le rfc record after this stamp. Verdict unchanged: enforced. Earlier judgement follows. Re-judged 2026-10-12 (independent auditor). SHIFTED by 4e731b2d96 (owner-approved lint-only reactor test edits). The tagged unit is byte-identical (gate-verified); the file-level changes are comment punctuation, slices.Concat over the same bytes, joined appends, strings.SplitSeq, newDefaultOriginatePeer taking its fixed addresses from constants with the same values, and registerTypeLenRecognizer losing a lo every caller passed as 1, none of which changes what a helper this unit calls produces. Verdict stands. Positives: sendInitialRoutes puts one End-of-RIB per negotiated family on the wire, including a silent family and a no-MP session. Negative TestRFC4724EndOfRIBNotSentBeforeTheInitialUpdateCompletes: while a plugin producing the initial update has not acknowledged peer-up, sendInitialRoutes is observed waiting and nothing is on the wire (EORSent 0); after the acknowledgement exactly the IPv4 unicast marker is written. Red on a marker sent ahead of the initial update or not sent after it. TestIsEndOfRIBAnyFamily is a neighbouring detector rule. Rejudged 2026-10-12 after commit ce62c78c3b moved peer_initial_sync_test.go around these units: the tagged functions there were re-read and are byte-identical, their assertions and fixtures still carry the evidence this note cites, and the other cited units did not change, so the verdict stands. Rejudged 2026-10-12 after 7a637d6df5 renamed SendUpdateHeld to sendUpdateHeld in two comments of peer_initial_sync_test.go: every tagged unit cited here is byte-identical (gate-verified), the comment edits sit outside them, and the assertions and fixtures still carry the evidence this note cites, so the verdict stands.
